headline: Ship Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry: the cheapest configuration that clears the pass-rate gate by more than noise, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1|usd_whole} a month.
lede: It passes {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} of tasks, its whole interval above the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate. The cheaper low-reasoning setting passes only on its estimate, by {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.distance|abs} points; if the gate is meant that way, it saves {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs} a month.

caveats.material_if: Only if the choice is meant relative to the planner now in production, which was not run; the gate is absolute and every configuration is read against it.
Only for the low-reasoning alternative, whose interval {spread.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval} straddles the gate; the recommendation clears it on its whole computed interval.

If the recommendation's clearance of {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.overall.distance|abs} point is mostly selection luck among {n_candidates|words} configurations, so a fresh case set reads it below the gate.

decision.text: Ship Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry. It passes {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean} of tasks, clear of the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate on its whole interval, at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.high.r1} per thousand calls ({cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1|usd_whole} a month).

Brisk-S with low reasoning and one retry is the cheapest configuration that passes on its estimate, and so the declared rule's pick, but it clears by {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.distance|abs} points: a fresh run this size would read it below the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time, and settling it would take {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.cases_needed_two_sided} cases. High reasoning instead costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs} more a month.

Atlas-M: no setting is separated from Brisk-S at the same settings, and its cheapest passing setting costs {cost_per_month.atlas-m.low.r1|usd_whole} a month. Nano-XS: no setting reaches the gate; its best passes {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean}.

The pick is the best of {n_candidates|words} configurations near one line, so a fresh case set may read it lower; if today's estimate is the truth, a fresh run this size reads it below the gate {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.overall.wrong_side} of the time. Multi-hop questions are its weakest task at {task.multihop.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.mean}, and its slow tail reaches {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}.

Confirm the pick on a fresh case set of today's size; if it holds above the gate, ship. In parallel, the gate's owner says whether the gate is read on the estimate, which decides whether the low-reasoning setting is eligible.

claims.text: Of the {n_candidates|words} configurations, {count.passing.pass_rate|words} reach the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass-rate gate, and the two Brisk-S ones with reasoning and a retry cost a fraction of the three Atlas-M ones.

evidence.caption: Cost per thousand calls, on a log axis, against pass rate for every configuration; the gate is {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}.

claims.text: Only high reasoning clears the gate by more than noise: its interval's lower end is {spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.low}, while low reasoning sits on the line at {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}.

evidence.caption: Pass rate with its computed interval against the gate, for the configurations nearest it.
How often a fresh run of today's size would read each on the other side of the gate, and the cases it would take to settle.

claims.text: Atlas-M is not separated from Brisk-S at the same settings, so its extra cost buys nothing measurable: the best Atlas-M setting costs {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs} more a month than the pick.

evidence.caption: Pass-rate change from moving the model or the reasoning level alone, with a retry on, with unpaired intervals; the step from low to high reasoning is not separated either.

claims.text: Multi-hop questions are where low reasoning falls short, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} against {task.multihop.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.mean} with high reasoning.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the two Brisk-S settings with a retry; task figures state no case counts, so they are descriptive.
A kept multi-hop failure of low reasoning: two hops collapsed into one search.

claims.text: High reasoning lengthens the slow tail to {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} from {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95}, still well under either Atlas-M setting.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to slow tail; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: How the pass-rate gate is read
explore.binds: High or low reasoning on Brisk-S
explore.outcome: Read on the estimate, low reasoning passes and saves {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs} a month; read on the whole interval, only high reasoning among the Brisk-S settings clears it, its lower end at {spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.low}.

explore.binds: Which configuration is cheapest to pass
explore.outcome: Up to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.low.r1.value}, Nano-XS with low reasoning and a retry, and cheaper Nano-XS settings below that; to {criteria.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.value}, Nano-XS with high reasoning and a retry; to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.value}, Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry; to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.value}, Brisk-S with low reasoning and a retry; to {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.value}, the pick; to {criteria.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.value}, Atlas-M with high reasoning and a retry; above that, nothing passes.

explore.binds: How far up the cost frontier to go
explore.outcome: Low to high reasoning on Brisk-S costs {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month per point; Brisk-S to Atlas-M at high reasoning costs {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month per point. Neither step's gain is separated from zero; the first buys distance from the gate, not a measured improvement.

omitted.why: A retry lifts every model and reasoning level at a small cost, and every Brisk-S survivor already carries one; it doesn't change the call.
Retry and reasoning effects don't differ between Atlas-M and Brisk-S; Nano-XS gains more from a retry but still misses the gate.
None reaches the gate; they appear in the scatter and the appendix.
Small differences between configurations; describes planner behaviour, not a decision axis.
The snapshot holds no figures for them.

omitted.what: Atlas-M with high reasoning and no retry
omitted.why: Passes on its estimate with an interval crossing the gate, and costs more than either Brisk-S survivor.

next.text: Re-run Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry, with the low-reasoning setting beside it, on a fresh set of {scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases} tasks.
next.settles: Whether the pick's clearance survives selection among many configurations; if it reads below the gate, Atlas-M with low reasoning and a retry is the next cheapest option clear of it.

next.text: The gate's owner declares whether the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate is read on the estimate or on the whole interval.
next.settles: Whether low reasoning, {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_cost_gap|abs} a month cheaper, is eligible.

next.text: Teach the low-reasoning planner to split multi-hop questions into steps, then re-test Brisk-S with low reasoning and a retry.
next.settles: Whether the cheaper setting can clear the gate with room; more cases alone would need {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.overall.cases_needed_two_sided}.

next.text: Record case counts per task in the next run.
next.settles: Whether the multi-hop shortfall is real or noise.

method.text: Each configuration ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases} tasks once, with none lost. The snapshot doesn't say whether every configuration ran the same tasks, so differences are read unpaired.
The snapshot does not define what makes a task pass; its kept failures are scored for a missing call, wrong arguments or the wrong tool.
The one declared criterion: pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} overall. It is read on the estimate as declared; the recommendation is also read on its whole interval.

{spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.level} intervals computed from each rate's binomial spread over its cases. Differences between configurations combine two spreads as independent, with no correction for the many comparisons.
How often a fresh run of today's size reads the other side of the gate, assuming today's estimate is the truth, at {settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.overall.level}.
Cost per thousand calls as measured; monthly cost at the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month} a month.
Median and slow-tail latency per configuration; no budget was declared, so it is descriptive.
No production planner was run, so nothing is read against current behaviour.
